title: Ecological Footprint
definition: A resource accounting tool that measures the biologically productive land and sea area required to provide the resources a human population consumes and to absorb its corresponding waste, using prevailing technology.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for GS Paper III (Environment & Ecology) and GS Paper I (Geography). Frequently linked to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), climate change mitigation, and resource management policies.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Ecological Footprint.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
